name: Holy See (Vatican City)
system_note: An elective monarchy in which the pope holds full legislative, executive and judicial power.
snapshot: The first American pope, Leo XIV, made artificial intelligence the theme of his first encyclical and declared the traditionalist Society of St Pius X in schism.
culture: The Vatican, the world's smallest state, holds St Peter's Basilica, the Sistine Chapel and one of the greatest art collections ever assembled. Latin remains its official language. The Swiss Guard, in uniforms said to have been designed in the Renaissance, has protected the pope since 1506.
society: The Holy See leads a church of about 1.4 billion people, growing fastest in Africa and Asia while shrinking in Europe. Pope Francis's reforms of Vatican finances and the curia, and the abuse scandals that shook the Church, framed the inheritance of Leo XIV, elected in May 2025, who spent much of his career in Peru.
situation: In May 2025, the cardinals chose the first American pope: Robert Prevost of Chicago, an Augustinian missionary who spent much of his career in Peru, who took the name Leo XIV. The name was a deliberate signal. The last Leo, Leo XIII, wrote the 1891 encyclical on the rights of workers in the industrial revolution. In 2026, Leo XIV made clear that he sees artificial intelligence as his era's equivalent.

He signed his first encyclical, ("Magnificent Humanity"), on 15 May, the 135th anniversary of , and the Vatican published it on 25 May (Catholic World Report). It warns of a "culture of power" fuelled by the digital revolution and AI and argues that technology must serve human dignity; the Vatican invited AI researchers, including Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah, to its presentation (Today, Explained via Podcast Rex). He has since chosen AI and war as the theme of the 2027 World Day of Peace. The year's other test came from the traditionalist Society of St Pius X, which rejects the reforms of the Second Vatican Council. On 1 July, despite the pope's personal plea to "please turn back," it consecrated four bishops in the same Swiss meadow at Écône where its founder did so in defiance of Rome in 1988. The next day the Vatican declared the group in schism and excommunicated the bishops involved, reversing the outreach of Benedict XVI and Francis (EWTN via Herald Malaysia).
power: An absolute elective monarchy. The pope, elected for life by cardinals under 80, holds full legislative, executive and judicial power over the Vatican City State and the worldwide Catholic Church of 1.4 billion members, governing through the Roman Curia.
holders: Pope Leo XIV, since May 2025; Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin.
